## Forecast pipeline

```{mermaid}
flowchart TD
    A[Today's real chlorophyll +<br/>6 covariates: temp_1m, cond_1m,<br/>temp_20m, sal_20m, cond_20m, air_temp]
    A --> Q{Is today's chlorophyll<br/>above 5 ug/L?}

    Q -->|Yes -- bloom in progress| BM[3 Random Forests trained only<br/>on past bloom events, using:<br/>days since bloom started, rise rate<br/>so far, day of year, recent forecast<br/>surprise, each covariate's own<br/>7-day trend, within-day chl-a volatility]
    BM --> BM1[Predict remaining peak magnitude]
    BM --> BM2[Predict remaining duration]
    BM --> BM3[Predict decline rate]
    BM1 --> TRAJ[Build trajectory:<br/>rise to predicted peak,<br/>then decline at predicted rate]
    BM2 --> TRAJ
    BM3 --> TRAJ
    TRAJ --> OUT[7-day chlorophyll forecast]

    Q -->|No -- calm| CFC[6 per-covariate Random Forests<br/>forecast each covariate forward,<br/>one day at a time, 7 days ahead]
    CFC --> CM[Calm-branch Random Forest:<br/>predicts tomorrow's chlorophyll<br/>from today's value + the 6<br/>forecasted covariates]
    CM -->|Repeat using<br/>yesterday's prediction<br/>as today's state| CM
    CM --> OUT
```

Every model here is retrained from scratch each day on all historical
data up to that point -- nothing is persisted between days except the
growing observation record and each day's forecast output. Which
chlorophyll model runs depends on whether today's real chlorophyll is
currently above or below the bloom threshold (5 ug/L):

- **Bloom day**: three Random Forests, trained only on past bloom
  events, each predict one property of how the current bloom will
  play out -- how high it will still peak, how many more days it
  will last, and how fast it will decline afterward. These use
  today's real covariate readings and each covariate's own 7-day
  trend directly, not a multi-day forecast of them, since the whole
  trajectory is predicted in one shot rather than day by day.
- **Calm day**: the 6 covariates are first forecast forward a day at
  a time (their own simple Random Forests, today's value + day of
  year predicting tomorrow's value), since a calm-day forecast
  genuinely needs to know what conditions will look like on each
  future day. A single Random Forest then recursively predicts each
  day's change in chlorophyll from the day before, using that day's
  forecasted covariates.
